phrase:
I’m digging through the trash
For a hard drive
note: In 2013 James Howells, a Welsh IT worker, discarded a hard drive that held the keys to about 8,000 bitcoin. He later tried to excavate a Newport landfill to find it; UK courts blocked that in 2025.

phrase: Heading to El Salvador
note: El Salvador made bitcoin legal tender in 2021, a world first. After an IMF-linked reform in 2025, businesses no longer had to accept it; acceptance became voluntary.

phrase:
I’ll remember 12 words
From my past life
note: Twelve (or twenty-four) recovery words are a seed phrase: enough to rebuild a bitcoin wallet on any device. Keep them and the coins can outlive every phone and laptop you own.

phrase:
I’m like Walton when he fucks
G spot order filled
note: Walton was a co-host on the Pleb Underground podcast who shared Bitcoin bars. He had a line punning 'G spot' (sexual innuendo) with 'spot order' (buying at the current market price), which Robbie borrowed.

phrase: With hopium from my cup
note: Hopium, hope plus opium, is crypto slang for comforting optimism that the price will pump. Here it also nods to Pleb Underground's hopium segments, where the podcast looks at positive news that could lift bitcoin.

phrase: Fudsters on the internet
note: FUD stands for fear, uncertainty and doubt. FUDsters spread scary claims about Bitcoin, sometimes sincerely, sometimes to shake people into selling.

phrase:
I’ll sell my diamond hands
To buy more sats
note: Diamond hands means holding through any crash without selling. Sats are satoshis, bitcoin's smallest unit: one hundred-millionth of a coin.

phrase: Stack ASICs on some tall racks
note: ASICs are computers built for one job: Bitcoin mining. Miners rack thousands of them, competing to add the next block of transactions and earn new bitcoin.

phrase:
If bears hibernate
I’m calling that a long nap
note: A bear market is a long stretch of falling prices. When the bears hibernate, the market goes quiet and sideways, sometimes for months.

phrase:
Half a milly
What hashrate foretells
note: 'Half a milly' means a US$500,000 bitcoin. Hashrate is the total computing power securing the network; bulls read rising hashrate as miners investing because they expect higher prices.

phrase: doof nights
note: A doof is Australian slang for a dance party with thumping electronic music, named after the 'doof doof' of the bass.

phrase: Got an orange pill
note: Being orange-pilled means becoming convinced about Bitcoin, a play on the red pill in The Matrix, with orange for Bitcoin's logo.

phrase:
Cause we just made toxic maxis
Radioactive
note: Toxic maxis are Bitcoin maximalists known for blunt, uncompromising defence of Bitcoin and rejection of other cryptocurrencies. Radioactive is the next level of toxic.

phrase: Fiat maxis disrespecting
note: Fiat maxis are people who trust only state-issued currency. They sit opposite Bitcoin maximalists on the money spectrum.

phrase: Sovereignty of individual
note: The Sovereign Individual (1997), by James Dale Davidson and William Rees-Mogg, argued that digital money would weaken governments' grip and shift power to individuals. Many Bitcoiners treat it as a prophecy.

phrase: Time thieves is the criminals
note: Your wages buy hours of your life stored as money. Inflation steals those hours by shrinking what the balance can buy, which is why Bitcoiners call money printers time thieves.

phrase:
Operate on block time
With ten minute intervals
note: Bitcoin adds a new block of transactions roughly every ten minutes. Block time is the network's own clock, counted in blocks rather than calendar dates.

phrase: Hashrate at an all time high
note: A record hashrate means more computing power than ever is protecting Bitcoin, making any attack on the network more expensive.

phrase: As we opt out and we exit
note: Opting out, or 'exit', means leaving a system instead of fighting it: moving savings from fiat into money no central authority controls.

phrase: Since the genesis
note: The genesis block is Bitcoin's first block, mined in January 2009. It contains a newspaper headline: 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'.

phrase:
Of a paper Nakamoto wrote
Just 9 pages to inspire
note: The Bitcoin white paper, published by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto on 31 October 2008, is nine pages long and describes the whole system.

phrase: Kiss on my baby pupusa
note: Pupusas are El Salvador's national dish: thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans or pork.

phrase: Martin had a dream
note: Martin Luther King Jr delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963, calling for equal treatment. The Bitcoin echo is one monetary rulebook that applies the same way to every user.

phrase: Cold storage made a cooler
note: Cold storage means keeping bitcoin keys completely offline, on a hardware wallet or written down, out of reach of online hackers.

phrase: Consensus to follow
note: Consensus is how thousands of independent computers agree on one shared record of who owns what: everyone runs the same rules, and no one is in charge.

phrase:
Because they tried
To tweak the model
note: Changing Bitcoin's rules needs broad agreement. In the block size wars, a push for bigger blocks failed to win users over, and its backers split off in 2017 to create Bitcoin Cash.
